title: Counting coordinates with large stable influence
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let $\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, suppose its variance under the product measure $\pi^n$ is at most $1$. For each coordinate $i$, define its stable influence at parameter $1-\delta$ by summing $(1-\delta)^{|\{j:a_j\ne0\}|-1}\widehat f(a)^2$ over all product Fourier indices $a$ with $a_i\ne0$, where $\widehat f(a)$ is the product Fourier coefficient. If $0<\delta<1$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1$, then the number of coordinates whose stable influence is at least $\varepsilon$ is at most $1/(\delta\varepsilon)$.
